title: Fletcher's wife Leora, the Smith Brothers and Joe Smith
summary: Scott tells how Leora, formerly married to Russell Smith, got Joe Smith into the band and Scott received his notice.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Well, it's a funny thing about Fletcher. Can I say something personal?
Fletcher married a woman that was a

trumpet player. She had played trumpet in Lafayette Theatre. They had shows, and she was in a women's band they had up there one time, a ladies' band. She played trumpet. And she had been married to a trumpet player, Russell Smith. Did you ever hear about the Smith Brothers?

Yeah. Well, these fellows -- we used to call them -- there were three of them. And all of them came -- originally there was six of them, they came from out West someplace. But three of them got to New York. And this Russell Smith, he was a good showman and all like that, but he was no good in a dance band.

He played the shows. He played in Lou Leslie's Blackbirds one year, and other shows. Then there was Luke. Luke, he was interested in pool. He was one of the best pool players. He could beat the world's best pool shark, too. But he was a good trumpet player. But he wasn't interested in music. Then there was Joe Smith.

Now, Joe couldn't read much, but he had a nice, beautiful tone. And Fletcher's wife liked Joe, the baby. He was -- all this was trumpet, now. She and Russell Smith broke up. She married Fletcher. But Joe still hung around and all like that. She influenced Fletcher, she let Joe come in the band.
Well, I was so busy, I had never -- I had seen her

and all like that, but -- I guess she was jealous of me or something like that. But I was so busy I didn't have time to socialize much with women and all like that, although I could have, but I was too busy. I was rehearsing and making records and playing dates, and those days you were playing every night. I couldn't socialize much.

So, after we got through work, we always came to the Amsterdam, because you found out different things, what was going on with musicians. When they got off their jobs they'd come -- that was our organization, we'd come there. And that's about the (inaudible), and I did. Well, she influenced Fletcher to let Joe join the band. So Fletcher sent me a notice that after this week, my services wouldn't be required.
